: Full Hypothesis Test for a Proportion
According to the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME), approximately 82% of the U.S.
population has been infected with COVID-19 at least once as of July 2022. Assume that 387 residents of
Richmond, CA, are randomly selected and 329 had been infected. Can we conclude that Richmond, CA, has
had more COVID-19 infections? Use 0.05 significance for the hypothesis test.
In this problem we are asked to use a hypothesis test to determine if there is a higher proportion of
COVID-19 infections in Richmond, CA, than in the U.S.
: We are given the fact that 82% of the U.S. population has been infected with COVID-19, so this
is what we will assume to be true. The question asks if the proportion in Richmond is higher,
> 0.82. This is a right tailed test.
Sample evidence suggests the alternative is likely true.
